en: The *Devatāsūtra* (GBM 1542.5):

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery. Then a certain deity of surpassing beauty, when the night had passed, approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Having approached and bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One, she sat down to one side.
Then, by the power of that goddess’s radiance, the entire Jeta Grove was suffused with a sublime light.
Seated to one side, that deity at that time spoke this verse:
"What indeed is that sharpened weapon? Or what is the hālāhala poison? What indeed is the kindled fire? Or what is that dreadful darkness?"
The Blessed One said:
"Malicious speech is a sharpened weapon; passion is the hālāhala poison;
hatred is a blazing fire; and ignorance is that terrible darkness. (2)
The deity said:
"What indeed has been taken by a mortal, or what is that which has been cast away here?
What indeed is this impenetrable armor, or what is this sharp weapon here? (3)
The Blessed One said:
That which was taken up and that which was given by oneself—whatever was left behind at home—is the impenetrable armor of patience and the sharp weapon of wisdom in this world. 4.
The deity said:
"Who indeed is called a thief? What is considered wealth by the virtuous? And who in the world, including the gods, are said to be robbed? (5)
The Blessed One said:
"Discursive thought is a virtuous thief; the wealth esteemed by the wise is ethical conduct (*śīla*).
Those in this world by whom ethical conduct has been cast down have themselves been robbed. (6)
The deity said:
"Who indeed is to be known as truly happy? Or who is the Supreme Lord? Who is eternally adorned? And who is mocked? Tell me. (7)
The Blessed One said:
"One who has few desires should be known as happy; one who is contented is a supreme lord.
One who possesses moral discipline is eternally adorned, while one whose discipline has fallen away is a laughingstock. (8)
The deity said:
What is it that fire does not burn, and what is it that the wind does not shatter? And what is it that the waters do not moisten, even while flooding the earth? 9.
The Blessed One said: "Fire does not burn merit, nor does the wind destroy it; the waters do not moisten merit, even while flooding the earth. (10)
The deity said:
"What is it that kings and thieves, though exerting themselves and being prepared, are unable to seize from a woman or a man? (11)
The Blessed One said:
"Neither kings nor thieves, though they move about and exert themselves, are able to take away the merit of either a woman or a man. (12)
The deity said:
"Who is that affectionate kinsman, or who is the enemy of evil intent?
What is that terrible suffering, or what is the supreme happiness? (13)
The Blessed One said:
A compassionate kinsman is merit; one of evil intent is an enemy and sin;
the terrible suffering of hell is impure disposition; and pure disposition is supreme happiness. 14.
The deity said:
By what is this world covered? By what is the world brought under control?
Why does one abandon friends? Why does one not go to heaven? (15)
The Blessed One said:
"The world is shrouded by ignorance and brought under the sway of delusion;
through greed one abandons friends, and through attachment one does not go to heaven. (16)
The deity said:
What is that which is pleasant yet unwholesome? Or what is wholesome yet not pleasant?
What disease causes the most suffering? And who is that one supreme physician? 17
The Blessed One said:
"Sensual pleasures are pleasant but unwholesome, while liberation is wholesome but not pleasant.
Passion is a disease that causes affliction, and the Buddha alone is the supreme physician. (18)
The deity said:
By what do friends increase? By what are enemies pacified?
By what does one attain heaven? And by what does one go to liberation? 19
The Blessed One said:
Through renunciation friends increase; through loving-kindness enemies are pacified;
from ethical discipline one attains heaven, and through wisdom one goes to liberation. 20. (Ds; GBM 1544.8)
The deity said:
"Even now, you ought to sever this doubt of mine: who, utterly deceived, has gone from this world to the world beyond? (21)
The Blessed One said: "He who, while wealth was available, did not accumulate merit, has gone from this world to the next world utterly deceived. (22)
The deity said:
"Ah, after a long time indeed, I behold a Brahmin who has attained final nirvana, who has transcended all enmity and fear, and who has crossed over the worldly attachments. (23)
Having spoken thus, that deity,
having rejoiced and approved of the Blessed One’s words, bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and departed from the presence of the Blessed One.

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery. Then a certain deity of surpassing beauty, when the night had advanced, approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, she bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Now, by the power of that deity’s radiance—
The entire Jeta Grove was suffused with a sublime radiance;
seated to one side, that deity at that time spoke this verse:
"What is their conduct? What is their behavior? What are their virtues? By what action [do they attain this]? Who here are the wise? Which people go to heaven?
To her, the Teacher, the deity, explained: [The rest of the verse is missing from the source text.]
Listen, O Goddess, to me regarding those people who go to heaven:
those who abstain from taking life, who are virtuous in conduct, and who delight in self-restraint— those people who do not harm living beings are the ones who go to heaven.
